name: Bleed Cartography
description:
Bleed Cartography emerged from the practice of harvesting residual emotional data left behind in shared BCI relay nodes — the psychic 'stains' that linger after thousands of users have passed their grief, desire, or rage through the same neural junction. Composers, called Cartographers, map these emotional residues into dense sonic landscapes that listeners experience not merely as sound but as navigable interior spaces, each track functioning as a kind of psychogeographic atlas of collective human feeling.

The genre is defined by its layered architecture: sub-bass frequencies carry what practitioners call 'the bone memory' of crowd-sourced trauma, while mid-register melodic fragments are stitched from anonymized neural snapshots donated or unknowingly leaked by commuters, laborers, and the dying. Playback via neural feed produces the uncanny sensation of walking through someone else's grief as though it were a physical neighborhood. Live performances are rare and legally complicated, as prolonged exposure can trigger unwanted memory consolidation in sensitive listeners.
creator: various
tier_availability: Mid and Upper tiers; bootleg relay-node copies circulate in Lower tiers via illegal BCI patch markets
legality: Legal with content-disclosure warnings; live performance requires Neural Exposure Licensing in most Meridian 88 districts
audience: BCI-equipped adults seeking intense emotional catharsis; grief therapists use curated tracks clinically; underground empathy-tourism communities
cultural_impact: Bleed Cartography has forced Meridian 88's legal system to grapple with questions of emotional consent and psychic property rights, since the raw material of the genre is technically harvested from the involuntary neural residue of ordinary citizens. The genre has spawned both a thriving therapeutic subculture and a vocal protest movement — the so-called Clean Node Coalition — demanding regular purging of relay-node emotional data. Its most celebrated album, 'Overpass 7 Remembers Everything,' is credited with changing grief-counseling protocols across three mega-districts.
story_hooks: A Cartographer discovers a relay node containing neural residue that appears to be from a person officially listed as never having existed — the emotional signature is too coherent and too old to be accidental.
A grief therapist's patient begins experiencing memories that don't belong to them after prolonged Bleed Cartography exposure, memories that describe a corporate crime in forensic detail.

The Clean Node Coalition hires a fixer to destroy a Cartographer's archive, but the archive turns out to contain the only surviving emotional record of a mass-casualty event someone powerful wants forgotten.
